summary: Best value + fit: Pichestay (new 2025 3-room, 3 singles + queen + king, 3 min from Achasan Stn, est ~$1,020 total) or Kkukio House / THE SYUIM (3 queen beds each, est $840-900 total) — all give each man his own real bed for $140-170/night TOTAL, well inside the $150-220 target and 40-55% cheaper than the 3-separate-hotel-room baseline (3 rooms x $80-110 x 6 nights = $1,440-1,980). Cheapest-and-closest wildcard is Stay Yeondu (~$600 total, directly opposite Walkerhill) if its bed count verifies for 3 sleepers. Logistics note: the Grand Walkerhill runs a FREE shuttle every ~10 min to Gangbyeon Stn (Line 2) and Gwangnaru Stn (Line 5), so anything walkable to those two stations (options 2, 3, 5, 8) has an effectively door-to-door commute. Korea legality in brief: legal short-term rentals for foreign tourists are registered 'Foreign Tourist Urban Homestay' businesses; since late 2025 Airbnb delists unregistered Korean hosts, so surviving listings are mostly compliant — still confirm a registration number in the listing/host profile before paying, since unregistered bookings historically got force-cancelled near arrival.
caveats: Airbnb, Booking, Vrbo and 9flats all blocked live scraping (403/429/empty JS shells), so NO price is quoted-live: totals are estimates from indexed/cached rates and Gwangjin market data (Kayak: district avg ~$90 weekend / ~$203 weeknight; small Achasan whole-apartments from ~$86/night; one $175/night 3BR quote; Stay Yeondu $93/night as of Apr 2025). Sep 28-Oct 3 2026 falls in/near the Chuseok holiday window, which can push Seoul prices up and sell out family-size units early — book 2-3 months out. Kkukio House and the exact Achasan 3-room Airbnb URLs need confirmation in the live Airbnb app (aggregator-indexed only). Estimated totals include a typical cleaning/service-fee load of roughly 15-20% on top of base nightly; verify at checkout. Also verify each Airbnb shows a Korean registration number (Foreign Tourist Urban Homestay) to avoid forced cancellation.

summary: 8 ranked candidates for 7 nights, Oct 18-25 2026, family of 5. Top tier for the 'nice, not cheap' brief: (1) Old Town Duodecim (3BR/2BA, AC everywhere, sea-view balcony, inside the walls, est ~$400/nt), (2) Pjesnik/Poet's House (restored 16th-c stone townhouse, 3BR/4BA, 2 min from Pile), (3) Apartment Bianco (4BR/4BA, 10 m off Stradun, published EUR 328-518/nt band, direct-book, easily fits a 6th bed). Best quiet-with-views alternates: Casa Bianca Elite and Croatian Villas DU206 in Ploce (Old Town/Lokrum views, 10-13 min walk in; Casa Bianca even has a lift + parking). Croatian Villas publishes real October rates (DU198 GBP 230/nt intra-muros, DU206 GBP 215/nt Ploce) — those anchor the market: genuinely nice 3BRs run ~$275-425/nt in late Oct, squarely inside the $200-400 guide. Value picks: Old Town Grand Terrace (3BR/2BA sleeps 8, ~$200/nt if live) and the 9.6-rated 15th Century 2BR/2BA (sleeps exactly 5, ~$178/nt).
caveats: Airbnb and Booking.com blocked direct scraping (403/empty renders), so Airbnb-native prices are snapshots or estimates — all price_confidence labels are honest; only the two Croatian Villas listings have published Oct 2026 seasonal rate cards. Add ~EUR 1.20-2.65 pp/night residence tax, platform service fees, and (agencies) a booking fee + EUR 200 arrival deposit to totals. Old Town practicalities: zero vehicle access inside the walls — taxis/transfers drop at Pile or Ploce Gate and you roll luggage over marble streets and often up stairs (most intra-muros units are walk-ups; the Vrbo 15th-century unit is street-level, Casa Bianca has a lift). Airport is ~30-40 min by car (~EUR 40-50 taxi). Split as a day trip is rough from Dubrovnik: 4-4.5 hrs each way by road crossing the Bosnia (Neum) corridor or via the Peljesac bridge, and the Krilo/TP-Line coastal catamaran typically ends its season in late October — if Split matters, plan an overnight or do Kotor/Montenegro (2 hrs) or Mostar (2.5 hrs) day trips instead. Late Oct = shoulder season: pleasant ~18-20C days, some rain risk, town uncrowded, availability genuinely easy — booking 2-3 months out is fine, but the named premium units (Duodecim, Pjesnik, Bianco) are one-of-a-kind and worth locking earlier.

summary: Airbnb is effectively OFF THE TABLE for this lane and that is a feature, not a gap: URA bans stays under 3 consecutive months in ALL private residential property (Planning Act; hosts fined up to S$60k in precedent cases), enforcement intensified 2024-25, and F1 week is peak crackdown season — any whole-home Airbnb near Marina Bay carries real last-minute-cancellation risk with no recourse during a sold-out week. Airbnb's own search also blocked headless fetching (403), so nothing listing-level could be verified as licensed. The legal hunt therefore produced two winning shapes. (1) BUDGET WIN, hits the $250-450/night target: 3 premium capsules at KINN (~$300/night total, 15-min WALK to MBS) or The Pod Beach Road (~$275/night, 1 MRT stop to circuit gates), with Dream Lodge (~$200/night) as the absolute floor — total ~$1,200-1,800 for 6 nights vs ~$7,000 at the Hilton Orchard baseline. (2) COMFORT WIN, legal whole apartment: Citadines Balestier 2BR ~$350/night (commute tradeoff) or Citadines Rochor 2BR ~$500/night (direct Downtown-line ride to Bayfront), both Ascott aparthotels bookable nightly — verify the 6-night stay clears each property's booking engine since the URA serviced-apartment class technically has a 7-day minimum (Ascott city properties sell nightly under hotel licensing; worst case book 7 nights). lyf Funan 2BR (~$575/night) is the location/culture pick for a crypto crew. All prices are surge-adjusted estimates (documented ~2-3x race-week multiplier on verified current baselines), not live quotes — the double event (Token2049's 25k attendees Oct 7-8 rolling straight into the first-ever Singapore SPRINT-format F1 weekend Oct 9-11) means whichever option is chosen should be booked immediately with free-cancellation terms.
caveats: Prices are NOT live quotes: Booking.com, Trip.com and Airbnb all refused to render date-specific rates to headless fetching, so every figure is an estimate built from verified current aggregator baselines x the documented ~2-3x F1-week surge (gpdestinations reader data; Mothership reported record Singapore ADRs in past F1 Septembers). Confidence labels reflect this. Second, this is a DOUBLE-surge week — Oct 4-7 is Token2049 pressure (25k+ attendees at MBS itself, 1,000+ side events) and Oct 8-10 is F1 pressure — so the low end of each range is optimistic. Third, the 6-night stay (Oct 4-10) sits one night under the URA 7-day serviced-apartment minimum; Ascott's lyf/Citadines city properties are generally hotel-licensed and sell nightly, but confirm at booking for Balestier/Rochor specifically, and budget for a 7th night (Oct 4-11) as fallback — note Oct 10-11 is race weekend proper so a 7th night also surges. Fourth, checkout Sat Oct 10 means the crew leaves the morning of F1 Saturday; if anyone stays for the race itself this whole lane needs re-pricing. Fifth, capsule options (KINN, The Pod) are adults-only with strict no-pod-sharing and 18+ check-in — fine for 3 male employees, but KINN is non-refundable inside 5 days and Token2049 has an official TravelSwap hotel-discount partner worth checking before booking anything (token2049.com/singapore/travel). Distances/transit minutes are map-typical; Oct 9-10 road closures around the circuit make MRT/walking the only reliable modes near Marina Bay, which favors the KINN/Pod/lyf Funan cluster and penalizes taxi-dependent Balestier.
